calls.head: The matchup inside the matchup
calls.body: The Golden Knights are one of the league’s best for chance quality, and the Kraken are one of the league’s best at preventing dangerous shots. We’ll side with the Golden Knights.
calls.call: The Golden Knights’ chances are more dangerous than the league average (a 6.3% chance of scoring on the average shot) against the Kraken.
calls.nums: Vegas 5th for chance quality (a 6.7% chance of scoring on the average shot) · Seattle 2nd for preventing dangerous shots
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 3 and 3 games this season
calls.happened: On chance quality, Vegas had 6.1% a shot. The league average is 6.3% a shot, and they came in at 6.7% a shot.

calls.head: The Kraken can’t afford to take penalties
calls.body: The Golden Knights’ power play is one of the league’s best, and the Kraken’s kill is near the bottom of the league. The Kraken need to stay out of the box.
calls.call: The Golden Knights’ power play creates at least their usual 8.9 expected goals per 60.
calls.nums: Vegas 2nd for power play (8.9 expected goals per 60) · Seattle 27th for penalty kill
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 3 and 3 games this season
calls.happened: Vegas’s power play created 11.8 expected goals per 60 in 5:50 of 5-on-4 time, against their usual 8.9, and scored 2 goals.

calls.head: The Golden Knights are going to test the Kraken’s goalie early and often
calls.body: Seattle has been giving up shots all season, and the Golden Knights rarely pass one up.
calls.call: The Golden Knights take at least their usual 59.2 shot attempts per 60 at 5-on-5.
calls.nums: Vegas 9th for shot volume (59.2 shot attempts per 60 at 5-on-5) · Seattle 32nd for shot suppression
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 3 and 3 games this season
calls.happened: Vegas took 69.0 shot attempts per 60 at 5-on-5 (adjusted for score and venue), against their usual 59.2.

SEA.head: We gave Seattle only a 28% chance, and it went the way we feared.

VGK.head: We gave Vegas a 72% chance, and Vegas delivered.

surprises.head: A rough night for J. Daccord
surprises.body: J. Daccord allowed 5 goals on shots worth 2.3 expected goals, 2.7 more than expected. Starting goalies had a night this rough about once every 20 starts over the last three seasons.

surprises.head: Seattle leaned on their bottom six
surprises.body: Seattle’s bottom-six forwards played 47% of the forwards’ 5-on-5 time, against their usual 43% and a league average of 42%. A team strays this far about once every 20 games.

story.head: The Golden Knights roll past the Kraken
paras: Victor Olofsson scored twice, opening the scoring midway through the first. Tomas Hertl added two power-play goals. Four different Golden Knights scored. Seattle pulled Joey Daccord after five goals.
The score was fair. Replay this game’s chances a hundred times and the Golden Knights win about seven in ten. By our Swing measure, Jack Eichel had the best night of anyone.

items.text: Two of the preview’s three calls held.
